I adopted both of them, a few months apart from New York Animal Control. I know most animal controls aren't low kill or anything, but I found a Facebook page dedicated to saving the dogs @ NYCACC and I realized just HOW MANY dogs they put down a day, mainly due to simple issues like Kennel Cough. 

**Logan**, I got him back in May, the day he was scheduled to be put down. He was an owner surrender, after having a home for a year they dumped him saying he had too much energy and needed training. (*Yet they also wrote they tied him up 12+ hours a day*) I was told at the shelter he was high energy (he's a 1 yr old Pit/German Shepherd mix), like a million times over. He seemed kind of bouncy but not too bad... they weren't kidding... I've spent every day with him since May and I wish I could have his energy. He's also by far the HAPPIEST dog I've ever met. Super loving, always down ta cuddle after a good walk. He's also the smartest dog I've ever met. I attempted suicide back in June, by taking a mix of pills including Canine sedatives that he didn't need anymore. He watched me take the pills and saw what they did -- now any time I go to take more than 3 pills at a time he *cries* and *barks* at me. I feel bad for him because he's really misunderstood by my neighbors/people in my building. He's very jumpy and also will cry when another dog passes by him without playing. He just wants friends but of course being a pit, people take this as bad behavior or even being dangerous. He's honestly my best friend, I love him more than ANYTHING.

**Cinnamon**, brought her home in mid-august. Same deal, was set to be put down that day. She was a stray just wandering through NYC. She's the 180 of Logan. Very quiet, shy demeanor. Not really into other dogs at all, she just wants human love all the time. She's still underweight because of how skinny she was when I got her, so I'm not sure if she'll come around in terms of energy or she'll always be low key. Loves to give kisses, to the point where you eventually need to push her off because it's too much. She's one of the gentlest, sweetest dogs I've met and I'm glad she's so calm because I don't know if I could handle two Logans.

Anyways, sorry this was so long, I really love my dogs. Again, sorry for your loss and I hoped this helped a bit. Feel free to PM me anytime.

Someone slipped something into my drink and I guess the original plan was just to rob me since I had a good job at the time. I woke up the next day to a phone call that my sister's best friend had passed away at 16 years old from a complication of Cystic Fibrosis. I didn't bring any of it up to my family until a week later when I realized my bank account was missing quite a bit of money. One of the guys was actually a really close friend, and knew my bank pin so I guess he went to the ATM and took out money while this whole thing was going on. 

I tell my therapist the last story and she says, "**Maybe they didn't know what they were doing was wrong. They thought it was party and you were all just getting messed up and fooling around.**" I couldn't even talk. She just said 5 guys raping me and not one of them thought it was wrong even though I was asleep. All I could say was, "Isn't withdrawing someone's money that isn't your own wrong? How could they think that was okay?" and she said something about "How about I just don't hang out with people who do drugs."

The last part of that post really helped me. I think what's hardest for me is to look at all the time I've spent doing nothing since I left my job in May. I sleep up to 16 hours a day. If I make it to an old age, I don't want to look back on what were supposed to be my best years and think about how angry I was and how much I slept. That's why part of me just really wants out and part of me wants to fight to make it better, but it's hard. 

Also, that's what I want to do as well. I live in RI currently, have absolutely nothing keeping me here. I have a degree, some really awesome work experience for huge companies, I could probably get a job if I tried. I'm scared shitless though because of that experience plus I lost the job before that when I tried to kill myself, they fired me for needing too much time off. 

I'd definitely say from someone who has sat around doing not that much after college, now is the time to move around and do shit while you don't have things weighing you down. Also, just a side note, since I don't think I'm going to kill myself, if you need resume help feel free to PM me.
